pages.en:
—Light streams in.

Even through my closed eyelids, I can feel the light announcing the arrival of morning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Light flows in.
The warmth I feel through my eyelids informs me that it is morning.

“Mmm——”

Sleep still clings to me.

Judging by the chill outside, it must be around half past five.

“Hm
”

pages.en:
“————”

I did not get to sleep until late last night.

After Saber and I returned from the church, I confined her to a room in the detached wing and finally went to bed sometime after three.

…Getting only two hours of sleep cannot possibly be healthy.

Yesterday was exhausting enough without that, with one crisis following another.

Surely no one will punish me if I sleep another half hour today—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
I went to bed late last night.
I came home from the church, forced Saber to sleep in the other building, and finally went to sleep myself around 3AM.
…I don’t know if I can cope with getting only two hours of sleep.
It was a frenetic, exhausting day yesterday.
Nobody can blame me if I sleep for another 30 minu

Men have… various complications upon waking too.

no, I stop myself at the last second.

pages.ja: 「それなのですが、やはり問題があります。部屋には案内されましたが、あそこはシロウの部屋から離れすぎています。貴方の身を守るには、常に傍に控えているのが適切です」
pages.jaRuby: 「それなのですが、やはり問題があります。部屋には案内されましたが、あそこはシロウの部屋から離れすぎています。貴方の身を守るには、常に傍に控えているのが適切です」
pages.en: “That is precisely the problem. You did show me to a room, but it is too far removed from your own. If I am to protect you, the proper course is to remain constantly at your side.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Yes, and I think there is a problem with it. You directed me to a room, but that room is not close enough to yours. I need to be by your side so that I may protect you.”

“?”

“…?”
Saber looks at me with wonder.

pages.en:
—Honestly, what does she imagine a healthy teenage boy is made of?

Her coming near me makes me nervous at the best of times. If she kneels right beside me at this hour of the morning, the shock alone will kill off brain cells. And with no warning at all! Under ordinary circumstances, my entire platoon of reason would have been wiped out.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Man, what does she think of a healthy guy of my age!?
I get nervous from just having her close to me, so it’s really shocking if she’s sitting by my side when I wake up. And it was a surprise attack too! If my composure were an army, that would’ve just annihilated it.

Saber’s argument is perfectly reasonable, but I wish she would consider my peace of mind as well.

If I slept in the same room as Saber, my sanity would collapse long before an enemy ever arrived.

No, more importantly, Saber cannot possibly remain with me every moment of the day. We need to establish some sense of appropriate distance—
